# Historical uploaded benchmark results — NOT generated by the revised code

These measurements were extracted from the `outputs/metrics.json` and `outputs/conversion_metrics.json` files in the source ZIP. They are supplied **as historical evidence only**: both files say generated **2026-08-31** and use the earlier **70% training / 30% holdout** protocol, which selected the apparent winner using the reported test holdout. The new code instead selects with validation and reports an independent 20% test; therefore **do not attribute any historical learner ranking numbers to the revised code**.

| Measure | Historical original value |
| --- | ---: |
| Criteo v2.1 rows scanned | 13,979,592 |
| Treatment-assigned / control-assigned rows | 11,882,655 / 2,096,937 |
| Overall assignment ratio | 85.000013% |
| 12-feature maximum absolute standardized difference | 0.04884 |
| Visit rate (control / treatment) | 3.82010% / 4.85434% |
| Visit ITT (absolute) | +1.03424 percentage points |
| Visit ITT (relative to control) | +27.07% |
| Visit 95% normal CI (absolute effect) | +1.00556 to +1.06292 percentage points |
| Conversion rate (control / treatment) | 0.19376% / 0.30895% |
| Conversion ITT (absolute) | +0.11519 percentage points |
| Conversion ITT (relative to control) | +59.45% |
| Conversion 95% normal CI (absolute effect) | +0.10845 to +0.12192 percentage points |
| Modeling sample / old holdout | 1,000,000 / 300,000 rows |

### Historical AUUC, as reported by the older code (not fair winner estimates)

| Outcome | S-learner | T-learner | X-learner |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Visit separate-relative AUUC | 0.01008745 | 0.00979894 | 0.00977308 |
| Conversion separate-relative AUUC | 0.00099512 | 0.00084345 | 0.00101528 |

The corresponding *apparent* winners were S-learner for visits and X-learner for conversions. Because the winning models were selected on the same holdout used to report these scores, the rankings must be treated as exploratory. Rerun with the revised three-way split before citing model-specific test AUUC.

**Interpretation:** These are effects of assignment on outcomes within a particular anonymized benchmark release; neither relative lift nor any policy diagnostic is evidence that a live advertising campaign was improved by that percentage. The pooled trials, nonuniform sampling and lack of experiment IDs limit external and design-level interpretations. A reported p-value of `0.0` reflects floating-point underflow, not literal zero probability.
